sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the late 1800s, as more and more people began to have electric lights in their homes,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末，随着越来越多的人开始在家里使用电灯，

sentences.en: the utility companies began looking for a good way to measure how much electricity each customer was using.
sentences.zh: 公用事业公司开始寻找好办法来计量每个客户消耗了多少电量。

sentences.en: Actually, way back when Thomas Edison built the first electric power stations,
sentences.zh: 事实上，早在托马斯·爱迪生建造第一座发电厂的时候，

sentences.en: there were no electric meters in people's homes.
sentences.zh: 人们家里并没有电表。

sentences.en: So he billed a monthly fee based on how many light bulbs they had.
sentences.zh: 所以他是根据他们拥有的灯泡数量来收取月费的。

sentences.en: That's Sam Evans-Brown of New Hampshire Public Radio.
sentences.zh: 这是新罕布什尔公共广播电台的萨姆·埃文斯-布朗。

sentences.en: That billing per light bulb system wasn't great, so people came up with a meter that did the job well enough.
sentences.zh: 按灯泡收费的系统并不太好，于是人们发明了一种能很好胜任这一工作的电表。

sentences.en: It's the same basic meter that most of us in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在美国大多数人

sentences.en: have in our homes today.
sentences.zh: 今天家里都有的那种基本电表。

sentences.en: And the way it works is when the electricity comes into your house,
sentences.zh: 它的工作原理是，当电流进入你家时，

sentences.en: a little dial turns forward and shows how much you've used.
sentences.zh: 一个小表盘会向前转动，显示你用了多少电。

sentences.en: And even though the original designers never really intended for this to happen,
sentences.zh: 尽管最初的设计者从来没真正想过会发生这种情况，

sentences.en: if you send electricity back into the grid, the dial turns backward to show electricity leaving your house.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把电送回电网，表盘就会倒转，显示离开你家的电量。

sentences.en: Now, if you're like me, there's no electricity leaving your house.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你像我一样，是没有电离开你家的。

sentences.en: It's only coming in.
sentences.zh: 电只进不出。

sentences.en: But if you're like Sam, who has solar panels on his roof,
sentences.zh: 但如果你像萨姆那样，屋顶上装了太阳能电池板，

sentences.en: electricity is leaving the house and going back into the grid.
sentences.zh: 电就会离开房子并流回电网。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's because my solar panels create more energy than I can use.
sentences.zh: 对，那是因为我的太阳能电池板产生的能量超过了我的消耗。

sentences.en: That excess energy goes back into the grid and out to my neighbors.
sentences.zh: 多余的能量会流回电网，并输送给我的邻居们。

sentences.en: And in my state, New Hampshire, I get credited for that extra energy I create.
sentences.zh: 在我的家乡新罕布什尔州，我产生的这些多余能量会得到信用额度补偿。

sentences.en: It's a practice called net metering.
sentences.zh: 这种做法被称为净计量。

sentences.en: And for a while, it was totally not controversial.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，这完全没有任何争议。

sentences.en: But now it is.
sentences.zh: 但现在有了。

sentences.en: There are huge political battles being fought over this.
sentences.zh: 围绕这个问题正在爆发巨大的政治斗争。

sentences.en: Sam and his colleagues at New Hampshire Public Radio actually did a whole episode of their podcast,
sentences.zh: 萨姆和他在新罕布什尔公共广播电台的同事们实际上为他们的播客做了一整集节目，

sentences.en: Outside In, about net metering because they are even nerdier than we are.
sentences.zh: 叫做《局内局外》，专门讨论净计量，因为他们比我们还要书呆子气。

sentences.en: And I'm actually just going to hand it off to them now.
sentences.zh: 实际上我马上就要把节目交给他们了。

sentences.en: So here's Sam.
sentences.zh: 所以接下来是萨姆。

sentences.en: And in a little bit, you'll hear the voices of his colleagues, Maureen McMurray and Taylor Quimby.
sentences.zh: 一会儿你还会听到他的同事莫琳·麦克默里和泰勒·昆比的声音。

sentences.en: So before we get into the controversy over net metering,
sentences.zh: 所以在我们深入探讨净计量的争议之前，

sentences.en: I want to go back and introduce you to the guy who accidentally started it all.
sentences.zh: 我想倒回过去，向大家介绍一下这个意外引发这一切的人。

sentences.en: His name is Stephen Strong.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫斯蒂芬·斯特朗。

sentences.en: Sun energy, the license plate, appropriately.
sentences.zh: 他的车牌很应景地写着“太阳能”。

sentences.en: Oh, and then we've got plug-in.
sentences.zh: 哦，然后我们还有插电式混合动力。

sentences.en: So like me, Stephen is an energy nerd.
sentences.zh: 所以和我一样，斯蒂芬也是个能源迷。

sentences.en: He's a guy who, when Toyota came out with the Prius, he got his engineers to hack the thing.
sentences.zh: 当丰田推出普锐斯时，他是那种会让自己的工程师去破解它的人。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: All right, so can you describe what we're looking at here?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你能描述一下我们在这里看到的是什么吗？

sentences.en: This is a lithium-ion battery pack that's shoehorned into the spare tire.
sentences.zh: 这是一个塞进备胎里的锂离子电池组。

sentences.en: So he and his engineers made a plug-in Prius, and they did it years before the car company.
sentences.zh: 所以他和他的工程师们制造了一辆插电式普锐斯，而且比汽车公司早了好几年。

sentences.en: And also Toyota went bananas when we told them we were doing this.
sentences.zh: 而且当我们告诉丰田我们在做这件事时，他们简直抓狂了。

sentences.en: So way back before he started messing around with Priuses, Stephen founded a company called Solar Design Associates.
sentences.zh: 早在开始瞎折腾普锐斯之前，斯蒂芬就创立了一家名为“太阳能设计联合”的公司。

sentences.en: This was at a time when solar power, besides being something on satellites in outer space, wasn't really a thing yet.
sentences.zh: 那是太阳能除了作为外太空卫星上的东西之外，还算不上什么实质事物的时代。

sentences.en: And when was this again?
sentences.zh: 这又是什么时候的事？

sentences.en: Is this the 70s?
sentences.zh: 是70年代吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, mid-70s.
sentences.zh: 对，70年代中期。

sentences.en: It was a heck of a hard way to make an easy living in the 70s and the 80s and the 90s.
sentences.zh: 在70、80和90年代，要在能源行业轻松谋生可真是一件难事。

sentences.en: So Stephen Strong is this hard-charging, ready-to-drop-everything-and-get-his-hands-dirty kind of guy.
sentences.zh: 所以斯蒂芬·斯特朗就是那种雷厉风行、随时准备放下一切并亲自动手的家伙。

sentences.en: And he kicked off what eventually became kind of a revolution in the way a lot of people are getting their energy.
sentences.zh: 他开启了后来在许多人获取能源方式上称得上是一场革命的浪潮。

sentences.en: He did it by putting solar panels on an apartment building for people with modest incomes.
sentences.zh: 他是通过在一栋中低收入人群的公寓楼上安装太阳能电池板来实现这一点的。

sentences.en: There it is.
sentences.zh: 就是那个。

sentences.en: That's the building there.
sentences.zh: 就是那栋楼。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 好大。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's huge.
sentences.zh: 对，好大。

sentences.en: With a Y.
sentences.zh: 带字母Y的那个。

sentences.en: Bernie.
sentences.zh: 伯尼。

sentences.en: Bernie's Y.
sentences.zh: 伯尼的Y（注：英文发音梗）。

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 好大。

sentences.en: So this building looks kind of like a big college dorm.
sentences.zh: 所以这栋楼看起来有点像大学里的大宿舍。

sentences.en: It's brick and pretty unremarkable.
sentences.zh: 它是砖砌的，很不起眼。

sentences.en: I think we're not supposed to drive this way.
sentences.zh: 我想我们不应该走这条路。

sentences.en: Well, that's the story of my life.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是我的人生写照。

sentences.en: But when it was built, on its roof there was this massive array of solar panels, one of the first of its kind.
sentences.zh: 但当它建成时，屋顶上有一大片太阳能电池板，是同类中最早的之一。

sentences.en: This was one of the largest solar thermal systems in New England, and it met something like 80% of the annual hot water requirements.
sentences.zh: 这是新英格兰最大的太阳能热水系统之一，它满足了大约80%的年度热水需求。

sentences.en: But this was like the early days of solar, so this is solar thermal.
sentences.zh: 但这就像太阳能的早期阶段，所以这是太阳能热水系统。

sentences.en: It's just like heating hot water.
sentences.zh: 它就像是加热热水。

sentences.en: It didn't make electricity.
sentences.zh: 它不发电。

sentences.en: Wait, so solar thermal uses solar panels, but all it does is heat up hot water, and that was cool?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以太阳能热水使用的是太阳能电池板，但它唯一的功用就是加热水，这居然很酷？

sentences.en: Solar thermal is like the simplest technology on the planet.
sentences.zh: 太阳能热水就像是地球上最简单的技术。

sentences.en: It's so simple.
sentences.zh: 它太简单了。

sentences.en: It's got this big box, and on the inside you've got some tubes that are colored black,
sentences.zh: 它有一个大箱子，里面有一些涂成黑色的管子，

sentences.en: and you put water in it or some sort of coolant or refrigerant in there,
sentences.zh: 你在里面注入水或者某种冷却剂或制冷剂，

sentences.en: and the sun shines on the black tubes and heats it up,
sentences.zh: 阳光照射在黑色的管子上并将其加热，

sentences.en: and then you can circulate that back into a tank, and that's all it was.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以把水循环回储水箱里，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: I feel like I could come up with that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我也能想出这个。

sentences.en: I feel like that's on the level technology-wise of using a magnifying glass to set a piece of paper on fire.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在技术层面上，这和用放大镜把一张纸点燃差不多。

sentences.en: Wait, the solar panels that Carter put on the White House, were those the solar thermal ones?
sentences.zh: 等等，卡特总统安在白宫屋顶上的那些太阳能电池板，就是这种太阳能热水板吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That was stupid.
sentences.zh: 那太蠢了。

sentences.en: That's it?
sentences.zh: 就这？

sentences.en: He was just heating water at the White House?
sentences.zh: 他只是在白宫里烧热水？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In any case, it was mostly solar thermal panels up there,
sentences.zh: 无论如何，上面大多是太阳能热水板，

sentences.en: but Stephen Strong convinced the developer to let him install a couple of solar photovoltaic panels, too.
sentences.zh: 但斯蒂芬·斯特朗说服开发商让他也安装了几块太阳能光伏板。

sentences.en: Photovoltaic panels are the ones that actually make electricity,
sentences.zh: 光伏板是真正能发电的板子，

sentences.en: and at that time they were a brand new technology.
sentences.zh: 在当时它们是一项全新的技术。

sentences.en: Now, as soon as the technology was available, we were employing it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，一旦这项技术可用，我们就在使用了。

sentences.en: But there was this question.
sentences.zh: 但当时有一个问题。

sentences.en: How should I do the wiring?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么走线呢？

sentences.en: Wait, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 等等，你什么意思？

sentences.en: So whenever the sun is shining, obviously the electricity will go towards running all the stuff in the building,
sentences.zh: 所以每当阳光普照时，很显然电力会流向运行大楼里的所有东西，

sentences.en: you know, water pumps, hot water heaters, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，水泵、热水器之类的。

sentences.en: But what happens when the sun's not shining?
sentences.zh: 但是当没有阳光的时候会发生什么？

sentences.en: Or what happens if the sun is shining and there's nothing going on in the building?
sentences.zh: 或者如果有阳光，但大楼里没有什么在运作，又会发生什么？

sentences.en: So what he decided to do was just configure it so that when there's no sun,
sentences.zh: 所以他决定进行配置，使得没有阳光的时候，

sentences.en: the building would work just like any other building.
sentences.zh: 这栋建筑的运作方式将和任何其他建筑一样。

sentences.en: It would buy electricity from the utility company,
sentences.zh: 它会向公用事业公司买电，

sentences.en: and the little dials on the electric meter would roll forward 5 kilowatt hours,
sentences.zh: 电表上的小表盘会向前转动5千瓦时、

sentences.en: 10 kilowatt hours, 20, 30, 40, 50.
I don't know what a watt.
sentences.zh: 我不知道什么是瓦特。

sentences.en: It's a watt of money.
sentences.zh: 这是一瓦的钱。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: A watt of money.
sentences.zh: 一瓦的钱。

sentences.en: You don't have to know what a watt is or what a kilowatt hour is.
sentences.zh: 你不需要知道什么是瓦特，也不需要知道什么是千瓦时。

sentences.en: You don't have to know.
sentences.zh: 你不需要知道。

sentences.en: All you need to know is that it's the measurement for electricity use.
sentences.zh: 你唯一需要知道的是这是用电量的计量单位。

sentences.en: So getting back to Stephen's solar panels,
sentences.zh: 所以回到斯蒂芬的太阳能电池板，

sentences.en: what he did that no one had ever done before was to wire it up
sentences.zh: 他做了一件前无古人的事情，那就是进行布线，

sentences.en: so that if the sun was shining and the building wasn't using any energy,
sentences.zh: 使得如果阳光灿烂而大楼没有消耗任何能量，

sentences.en: the unused electricity would flow out into the grid
sentences.zh: 未使用的电能就会流出到电网中，

sentences.en: and the little dial on the meter would just roll in the other direction, backwards.
sentences.zh: 电表上的小表盘就会朝另一个方向倒转。

sentences.en: Which means at the end of the month when the person comes to check the meter,
sentences.zh: 这意味着到了月底有人来查表时，

sentences.en: the owners of the building would pay for whatever the dial said.
sentences.zh: 大楼的业主只需为表盘显示的数字付费。

sentences.en: So like if they use 60 kilowatt hours, but they put in 40,
sentences.zh: 所以比如他们用了60千瓦时，但他们输入了40千瓦时，

sentences.en: the dial would say 20 and they would only pay for 20.
sentences.zh: 表盘就会显示20，他们只需要为20付费。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 而且它成功了。

sentences.en: It was just, it was intuitive.
sentences.zh: 它就是，它很直观。

sentences.en: It was almost like that's just the way it should be.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像事情本来就该是这样。

sentences.en: It's like we're producing electrons that are just as valuable
sentences.zh: 就像我们产生的电子和煤炭发电厂

sentences.en: as the ones provided by the coal plant or the heavy residual fuel oil driven plant.
sentences.zh: 或重质残油燃料发电厂提供的电子一样有价值。

sentences.en: Why shouldn't they receive the same value?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们不应该获得相同的价值？

sentences.en: And so it just made sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这讲得通。

sentences.en: I mean, did you talk to the utility at all?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你和公用事业公司沟通过吗？

sentences.en: Did you show them your design and say, this is what we're going to do?
sentences.zh: 你有没有把你的设计展示给他们看并说，这就是我们要做的？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: The developers, they said, don't, you don't worry about that.
sentences.zh: 开发商们说，别，你不用担心那个。

sentences.en: You just get the technical side of this done and get it, get it working.
sentences.zh: 你只管把技术方面搞定，让它运作起来。

sentences.en: And we'll, we'll take care of that.
sentences.zh: 我们会处理那部分的。

sentences.en: We're going to be interfacing with the utility.
sentences.zh: 我们会去和公用事业公司对接。

sentences.en: It turned out that they didn't say anything about the system to the utility purposefully
sentences.zh: 结果证明，他们故意没有向公用事业公司透露任何关于这个系统的信息，

sentences.en: and, and told me at the time, there's one thing in your career that you should learn early.
sentences.zh: 并在当时告诉我，你职业生涯中有一件事应该尽早学会。

sentences.en: And that is, it's easier to ask forgiveness than it is to ask permission.
sentences.zh: 那就是，请求原谅比请求许可更容易。

sentences.en: And that, ladies and gentlemen, is how we got a little policy called net metering.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，这就是我们如何得到一项名为净计量的政策。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So why wouldn't he tell them?
sentences.zh: 那他为什么不告诉他们呢？

sentences.en: Well, this is uncharted waters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是未知的领域。

sentences.en: He didn't know what the utility would say and he didn't want to be told no.
sentences.zh: 他不知道公用事业公司会怎么说，而且他不想听到拒绝。

sentences.en: So net metering, it's the net of when the meter goes forward and goes backward.
sentences.zh: 所以净计量，就是电表向前走和向后走的净差值。

sentences.en: It's what's in between.
sentences.zh: 这就是中间的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, net as in net versus gross.
sentences.zh: 对，这里的“净”是指净值对总值。

sentences.en: I mean, the only reason that it was designed that way is because that is what the meter could do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它之所以这样设计，唯一的理由就是那是电表能做到的。

sentences.en: You know, that little spinning disc electric meter.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那个带旋转盘的电表。

sentences.en: All it can do is spin forward and backwards.
sentences.zh: 它能做的就是向前转和向后转。

sentences.en: So that's what they used.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就用了这个。

sentences.en: But it was well and truly the first one that was connected to the utility grid
sentences.zh: 但它确实是第一块连接到公用事业电网的太阳能板，

sentences.en: outside the fence of a government laboratory.
sentences.zh: 而且是在政府实验室的围墙之外。

sentences.en: Okay, so he puts in the solar panels on the roof of this building.
sentences.zh: 好的，他在这个建筑物的屋顶上安装了太阳能电池板。

sentences.en: What, what happens?
sentences.zh: 什么，发生了什么？

sentences.en: So the utility company, they were actually fine with the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 所以电力公司，他们其实对整件事情都没什么意见。

sentences.en: In fact, they praised Stephen's innovation, but the solar panels didn't last very long.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们赞赏了斯蒂芬的创新，但太阳能电池板并没有维持很久。

sentences.en: They actually blew off the building in the first year.
sentences.zh: 它们在第一年就被风从大楼上吹掉了。

sentences.en: They didn't like, they didn't glue them on or whatever?
sentences.zh: 他们难道没有，没有把它们粘起来什么的吗？

sentences.en: It's Massachusetts, it gets windy.
sentences.zh: 这里是马萨诸塞州，风很大。

sentences.en: So not a terribly auspicious start, but what it did was kick off some intense interest in this idea
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一个特别吉利的开端，但它激发了人们对这个想法的极大兴趣

sentences.en: that solar could serve the needs of a home, but also produce electricity for the grid,
sentences.zh: 太阳能不仅可以满足家庭的需求，还可以为电网发电，

sentences.en: like a tiny part-time power plant.
sentences.zh: 就像一个微型的兼职发电厂。

sentences.en: And this concept of homeowner as power plant is actually important in thinking about how
sentences.zh: 而房主作为发电厂这个概念，在思考

sentences.en: people with solar panels on their homes will be paid for the power they're producing.
sentences.zh: 家房屋顶上有太阳能电池板的人将如何为其生产的电力获得报酬时，其实非常重要。

sentences.en: Because big established power plants sell power to the utility companies at a cheaper wholesale coSt.
sentences.zh: 因为大型老牌发电厂以更便宜的批发价将电力出售给电力公司。

sentences.en: And then the utility companies can sell their customers that power at a higher retail rate
sentences.zh: 然后电力公司以更高的零售价将这些电力出售给客户

sentences.en: so they can make profit and pay for their costs.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能获利并支付成本。

sentences.en: So then the question becomes, do people with solar panels, do they become like the mini power plants?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，拥有太阳能电池板的人，他们会变成微型发电厂吗？

sentences.en: Should they be paid the lower wholesale rate or the higher retail rate?
sentences.zh: 他们应该获得较低的批发价还是较高的零售价？

sentences.en: So are they like Costco or are they like mom and pop?
sentences.zh: 所以他们就像好市多（Costco）还是夫妻店？

sentences.en: Is that it?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Did I nail this analogy?
sentences.zh: 我这个比喻打得准吗？

sentences.en: I think that's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我觉得挺贴切的。

sentences.en: In any case, states eventually started passing laws about this very question.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，各州最终开始通过有关这个问题的法律。

sentences.en: And that was all through the 80s and the 90s.
sentences.zh: 这些都是在80年代和90年代进行的。

sentences.en: And for the most part, these laws said that the utility companies should pay people the higher retail rate
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，这些法律规定电力公司应该向人们支付更高的零售价

sentences.en: because it's expensive to put solar panels on your house and this would incentivize solar.
sentences.zh: 因为在屋顶上安装太阳能电池板很贵，而这会激励太阳能的发展。

sentences.en: And eventually, 41 states passed laws allowing people to get this higher retail rate for net metering.
sentences.zh: 最终，有41个州通过了允许人们在净计量电价中获得更高零售价的法律。

sentences.en: And utility companies, at the time, they didn't put up much of a fight about it.
sentences.zh: 而当时电力公司并没有进行太大的抗争。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the utility companies, at this point, they're like dancing with the devil and they don't even realize it.
sentences.zh: 对，但电力公司在这一点上，就像是在与魔鬼共舞，他们甚至都没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, and nobody had any reason to say, oh, this might not be a good idea
sentences.zh: 是的，而且当时没有人有理由说，哦，这可能不是一个好主意

sentences.en: because solar was just like this weird thing that probably was never going to be cost effective.
sentences.zh: 因为太阳能就像是一个奇怪的东西，可能永远都不会具有成本效益。

sentences.en: And that's how it was for a bunch of years.
sentences.zh: 好几年都是这样的情况。

sentences.en: Until, suddenly, solar started to get cheap.
sentences.zh: 直到突然之间，太阳能开始变便宜了。

sentences.en: For decades, solar power was so expensive and unwieldy, few could afford it.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，太阳能电力既昂贵又笨重，很少有人能负担得起。

sentences.en: And that is changing in a mind-bendingly rapid pace.
sentences.zh: 而这种状况正以令人眼花缭乱的速度改变着。

sentences.en: Solar-related stocks rallied on Wednesday on the news that Congress plans to extend a solar investment tax credit by five years.
sentences.zh: 周三，太阳能相关股票上涨，此前有消息称国会计划将太阳能投资税收抵免延长五年。

sentences.en: Starting in the mid-2000s, a bunch of really ambitious, well-financed companies started saying,
sentences.zh: 从2000年代中期开始，一帮雄心勃勃、资金充足的公司开始表示，

sentences.en: hey, we could make some money doing this.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们做这个能赚到钱。

sentences.en: And so from 2009 to 2010, the amount of solar in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，从2009年到2010年，美国的太阳能发电量

sentences.en: doubled.
sentences.zh: 翻了一番。

sentences.en: It doubled again from 2010 to 2011.
sentences.zh: 从2010年到2011年，它又翻了一番。

sentences.en: It doubled again from 2011 to 2013.
sentences.zh: 从2011年到2013年，它再次翻了一番。

sentences.en: And from 2013 to today, it's on track to triple again.
sentences.zh: 而从2013年到现在，它有望再次翻三番。

sentences.en: Okay, so what are these companies doing that's different?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那这些公司在做什么不同的事情？

sentences.en: Like how are they making money?
sentences.zh: 比如他们是怎么赚钱的？

sentences.en: What's their model?
sentences.zh: 他们的商业模式是什么？

sentences.en: What they're doing is they're offering people solar for no money down.
sentences.zh: 他们做的是为人们提供零首付的太阳能。

sentences.en: They pay for the cost of the panels.
sentences.zh: 他们支付电池板的费用。

sentences.en: In exchange, they take a chunk of the money that you would earn by producing power.
sentences.zh: 作为交换，他们拿走你通过发电本应赚取的一部分钱。

sentences.en: And so if you had someone come and knock on your door and say,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你遇到有人敲响你的门并说，

sentences.en: hey, want to be part of the next renewable energy era?
sentences.zh: 嘿，想成为下一个可再生能源时代的一部分吗？

sentences.en: And you could have solar panels on your roof right now and it's not going to cost you any money
sentences.zh: 你现在就可以在屋顶上安装太阳能电池板，而且不需要花你任何钱

sentences.en: and we're going to give you a discount on your power bill?
sentences.zh: 我们还会给你的电费打折？

sentences.en: I'd say, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我会说，行啊。

sentences.en: And that business model is made possible by net metering,
sentences.zh: 而这种商业模式是由净计量促成的，

sentences.en: by getting this higher retail rate for the power people are producing with solar.
sentences.zh: 也就是通过人们利用太阳能发电获得更高的零售价。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say that the utility companies basically did not see this coming.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，电力公司基本上没有预料到这一点。

sentences.en: And so now they're starting to push back.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他们开始进行反击了。

sentences.en: They don't want to be paying the retail rate.
sentences.zh: 他们不想支付零售价。

sentences.en: They think people generating electricity with solar should get the wholesale rate,
sentences.zh: 他们认为用太阳能发电的人应该获得批发价，

sentences.en: just like a power plant would.
sentences.zh: 就像发电厂一样。

sentences.en: So where are the fights happening now then?
sentences.zh: 那么现在争端在哪里发生呢？

sentences.en: Where are the really high profile fights over net metering?
sentences.zh: 关于净计量的备受瞩目的争端究竟在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, so obviously Arizona is the number one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然亚利桑那州排在第一位。

sentences.en: So that's Christy Schallenberger,
sentences.zh: 那是克里斯蒂·沙伦伯格（Christy Schallenberger），

sentences.en: who works for this industry news site called Utility Dive that tracks all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 她为一家名为Utility Dive的行业新闻网站工作，该网站追踪所有这些事情。

sentences.en: She points out that we've seen net metering battles in California.
sentences.zh: 她指出，我们在加利福尼亚州看到了净计量之争。

sentences.en: And of course you have Nevada,
sentences.zh: 当然还有内华达州，

sentences.en: which has basically become the byword for what you don't want to see.
sentences.zh: 它基本上成了你不想看到的局面的代名词。

sentences.en: Nevada's fight got really crazy.
sentences.zh: 内华达州的争端变得非常疯狂。

sentences.en: Huge, huge blowback from all walks of life.
sentences.zh: 来自各行各业的巨大强烈反对。

sentences.en: Basically, you have celebrities, you have presidential candidates.
sentences.zh: 基本上，有名人，还有总统候选人。

sentences.en: I do not often get involved in state or local issues other than my own state,
sentences.zh: 除了我自己的州之外，我一般不参与州或地方事务，

sentences.en: but I find it rather incredible that the Public Utilities Commission here in Nevada
sentences.zh: 但我发现内华达州的公共公用事业委员会做出了一个决定，

sentences.en: has made a decision which makes it harder for people to install solar panels.
sentences.zh: 这使得人们安装太阳能电池板变得更加困难，这实在是令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Wait, who was that?
sentences.zh: 等等，那是谁？

sentences.en: That was Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 那是伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）。

sentences.en: You're joking.
sentences.zh: 你在开玩笑吧。

sentences.en: But anyway, you've got this crazy obscure policy that's getting tons of attention.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，这个鲜为人知的晦涩政策获得了大量的关注。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton talked about it when she went to Nevada and talked to local newspapers there.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿（Hillary Clinton）去内华达州并与当地报纸交谈时谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: There are fights in Iowa, Texas, Maine, Vermont, New York, Utah, Hawaii,
sentences.zh: 爱荷华州、得克萨斯州、缅因州、佛蒙特州、纽约州、犹他州、夏威夷州都有争端，

sentences.en: and of course right here in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 当然还有我们这里的在新罕布什尔州。

sentences.en: It's a battle that's happening all over the country, state by state.
sentences.zh: 这是一场在全国范围内、各州之间上演的战斗。

sentences.en: The local electric companies pushing back and all the solar installers fighting against the utilities.
sentences.zh: 当地的电力公司在反击，所有的太阳能安装商都在与公用事业公司作斗争。

sentences.en: And each state has like its own local flavor to this argument.
sentences.zh: 每个州对这场争论都有其独特的本地特色。

sentences.en: But I still don't understand a little bit about this fight.
sentences.zh: 但我还是有点不理解这场争端。

sentences.en: Like, why would me having solar panels on my roof, why would it make the utility company like so angry?
sentences.zh: 比如，为什么我在屋顶上安装太阳能电池板，会让电力公司如此愤怒？

sentences.en: Is it just money?
sentences.zh: 难道只是为了钱吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, of course it's about money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，这当然是为了钱。

sentences.en: But who's money?
sentences.zh: 但这是谁的钱？

sentences.en: The utility companies want to reframe this argument so that it's not just about their interests,
sentences.zh: 电力公司想要重新构架这场争论，使其不仅关乎他们的利益，

sentences.en: but it's about the interests of the people who don't have solar panels.
sentences.zh: 而是关乎没有安装太阳能电池板的人的利益。

sentences.en: So, okay, here I talk to Michael Harrington, who here in New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，在这里我采访了迈克尔·哈灵顿（Michael Harrington），他在新罕布什尔州，

sentences.en: he used to be one of the guys who regulates electric companies.
sentences.zh: 他过去是监管电力公司的人员之一。

sentences.en: It's a taking from the not so, people that have not so much and giving it to people who have more.
sentences.zh: 这是从不太宽裕、拥有较少资源的人那里拿走东西，给那些拥有更多资源的人。

sentences.en: Say I was a retired school teacher in Manchester living in an apartment.
sentences.zh: 假设我是曼彻斯特的一名退休学校教师，住在一个公寓里。

sentences.en: There's no way I'm going to put solar panels on that apartment roof and get any benefit from that metering,
sentences.zh: 我绝不可能在那个公寓屋顶上安装太阳能电池板并从净计量中获得任何好处，

sentences.en: but I'm going to have to pay for it because some guy in Bedford, I just used Bedford as an example,
sentences.zh: 但我却不得不为之付钱，因为贝德福德的某个人——我只是把贝德福德当作一个例子，

sentences.en: got nothing to do with a problem with Bedford.
sentences.zh: 这跟贝德福德的问题没有任何关系。

sentences.en: Bedford, if you're not from New Hampshire, is a wealthy suburb of Manchester, which is our biggest city.
sentences.zh: 贝德福德，如果你不是新罕布什尔州人，它是曼彻斯特的一个富裕郊区，而曼彻斯特是我们最大的城市。

sentences.en: But he might have a 4,000 square foot house, and he says, boy, if I do this net metering thing,
sentences.zh: 但他可能拥有一栋4000平方英尺的房子，他说，天哪，如果我搞这个净计量，

sentences.en: in five or six years, I'll be getting basically free electricity.
sentences.zh: 在五六年内，我基本上就能获得免费电力了。

sentences.en: So it's a reverse distribution of wealth from the way we normally do things in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以这与我们在美国通常做事情的方式相反，是一种财富的逆向分配。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不对。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So it's like someone ultimately has to pay, and if all of these people who are people of means,
sentences.zh: 所以就像总得有人付钱一样，如果所有这些有钱人、

sentences.en: who are homeowners, have solar panels, then the cost of the other utility will go up.
sentences.zh: 也就是房主们都有太阳能电池板，那么其他公用事业的成本就会上升。

sentences.en: And that means that people who are renting or anything like that, they get screwed because I want solar panels on my house.
sentences.zh: 这意味着租房者或类似的人会吃亏，因为我想在我的房子上装太阳能电池板。

sentences.en: And that's me.
sentences.zh: 这就是我。

sentences.en: This is how rate structures work, right?
sentences.zh: 费率结构就是这样运作的，对吧？

sentences.en: A utility is a big company that invests a ton of money in poles and wires, in energy descent across those poles and wires,
sentences.zh: 公用事业公司是一家大公司，在电线杆和电线以及通过这些电线杆和电线传输的能源上投资了大量资金，

sentences.en: and then they take all of their customers and they divide the cost of that up between all of them and they spread it around.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将所有的客户召集起来，把这些成本在所有人中间进行分摊并均摊开来。

sentences.en: And under that business model, if, say, 50% of the people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而在这种商业模式下，比方说，如果美国有50%的人

sentences.en: went solar and started net metering,
sentences.zh: 改用太阳能并开始净计量，

sentences.en: a big chunk of the money that they're saving is money that's not going towards paying for the poles and wires.
sentences.zh: 他们所节省的一大笔钱就是那些本应用来支付电线杆和电线费用的钱。

sentences.en: So this is the argument against net metering, which is you, or let's say me, because I actually do have solar panels on my roof, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是反对净计量的论据，那就是你，或者我们假设是我，因为我的屋顶上确实有太阳能电池板，对吧？

sentences.en: So you're screwing me because I don't.
sentences.zh: 所以你在坑我，因为我没有。

sentences.en: I'm screwing you, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是我在坑你，对。

sentences.en: Me putting solar panels on my roof costs you money.
sentences.zh: 我在屋顶上安装太阳能电池板让你花钱了。

sentences.en: What the hell, Sam?
sentences.zh: 搞什么鬼，萨姆？

sentences.en: What the hell, Sam?
sentences.zh: 搞什么鬼，萨姆？

sentences.en: Except the problem is we're not 100% sure that's true.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们并没有百分之百确这是真的。

sentences.en: Hold on a second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: I've got to look something up because, um...
sentences.zh: 我得查证点东西，因为，嗯……

sentences.en: So this is another former regulator, Cliff Below.
sentences.zh: 所以这位是另一位前监管机构官员，克利夫·贝洛（Cliff Below）。

sentences.en: Where is that?
sentences.zh: 那是在哪里？

sentences.en: He's the one here in New Hampshire who wrote the first initial net metering law here in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 他就是新罕布什尔州这里起草新罕布什尔州第一部最初的净计量法的人。

sentences.en: Oh, well, I see the footnote to it.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，我看到它的脚注了。

sentences.en: And he says that even then, there was this intuition, like this feeling, that maybe there were actually benefits to solar.
sentences.zh: 他说，即便在那个时候，也有这样一种直觉，就像一种感觉，认为太阳能实际上可能是有好处的。

sentences.en: So the feeling was solar might be higher than average in value, and I think the evidence has proven that out over the years,
sentences.zh: 所以当时的感觉是太阳能的价值可能高于平均水平，我认为多年来的证据已经证明了这一点，

sentences.en: that solar tends to produce at higher than average price hours.
sentences.zh: 即太阳能倾向于在价格高于平均水平的时段发电。

sentences.en: So Cliff Below is literally saying the exact opposite thing from Michael Harrington.
sentences.zh: 所以克利夫·贝洛所说的话与迈克尔·哈灵顿的说法完全相反。

sentences.en: He's saying that me putting solar panels on my roof actually saves you guys money.
sentences.zh: 他说我在屋顶上安装太阳能电池板实际上为你们省了钱。

sentences.en: Okay, well, this is a pickle.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这下陷入两难了。

sentences.en: I don't know if I believe him.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否相信他。

sentences.en: I don't think it's going to save enough money.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它能省下足够的钱。

sentences.en: All right, so let's first maybe dig into why it might be.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们先来深入探讨一下这可能是为什么。

sentences.en: Even though we pay the same amount for every unit of energy on our electric bills, all electrons are not created equal.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们在电费账单上为每一单位能源支付相同的金额，但并非所有的电子都是平等的。

sentences.en: In reality, every five minutes, there's a new auction for energy.
sentences.zh: 现实中，每五分钟就会有一场新的能源拍卖。

sentences.en: So every five minutes, we've got a new price for energy.
sentences.zh: 所以每五分钟，我们都有一个新的能源价格。

sentences.en: When demand is low, prices are low, and they can actually go negative.
sentences.zh: 当需求较低时，价格就很低，甚至可能出现负数。

sentences.en: Like power plants will pay us so that they don't have to shut down.
sentences.zh: 就像发电厂会付钱给我们，这样他们就不用停工关机了。

sentences.en: Usually that's at night.
sentences.zh: 通常那是在夜间。

sentences.en: And when demand is high, prices can be insane, like 100 times higher than normal.
sentences.zh: 而当需求高时，价格可能会疯狂飙升，比正常水平高出100倍。

sentences.en: And again, the utilities take all of those costs, they average them all out, and they divide them by their customers.
sentences.zh: 同样，公用事业公司将所有这些成本加起来，取平均值，然后分摊给他们的客户。

sentences.en: So the thing is, solar panels are producing at times of day that's really high value.
sentences.zh: 所以关键在于，太阳能电池板是在一天中价值非常高的时段发电的。

sentences.en: Sunny, hot.
sentences.zh: 晴朗，炎热。

sentences.en: But those are usually the times where electricity is expensive, and that's when you're producing solar power.
sentences.zh: 但这些通常正是电力昂贵的时候，而这正是你产生太阳能电力的时候。

sentences.en: And so by feeding back into the grid, we're cutting usage so much that it lowers the price during those peak times.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过向电网回输电力，我们大量削减了用电量，从而降低了高峰时段的价格。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so Cliff Bilo is arguing these people are actually, you know, even though they're getting paid more than a regular power plant,
sentences.zh: 所以克利夫·贝洛的论点是，这些人实际上，你知道的，尽管他们获得的报酬比普通发电厂还要多，

sentences.en: they're actually getting paid less than the energy's worth.
sentences.zh: 他们实际拿到的报酬比能源本身的价值还要低。

sentences.en: And that means that there's savings for every solar panel you put on the grid.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你接入电网的每一块太阳能电池板都能节省开支。

sentences.en: I would admit, but that's only true up until a certain point, right?
sentences.zh: 我承认，但这只在某种程度上成立，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, if you suddenly tip it and it goes from 20% of the population on solar panel to 50 to 70, then I'm sorry, Cliff, your math doesn't work out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你突然扭转局势，太阳能发电人口从20%飙升到50%甚至70%，那我很抱歉，克里夫，你的数学行不通了。

sentences.en: That is exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: You should go work for MIT.
sentences.zh: 你应该去麻省理工学院工作。

sentences.en: So people do have ideas about how to solve all of this, which we can talk about, or we could not.
sentences.zh: 所以人们确实对如何解决所有这些问题有想法，我们可以讨论，也可以不讨论。

sentences.en: Give us one.
sentences.zh: 说一个听听。

sentences.en: Give us your favorite.
sentences.zh: 说一个你最喜欢的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, the most interesting to me is from a guy called Don Kreese.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我最感兴趣的是一个叫唐·克里夫的人提出的。

sentences.en: Do you think that the way that we pay for electricity is just dumb?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们支付电费的方式是不是很蠢？

sentences.en: It's a leading question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个带有引导性的问题。

sentences.en: Yes, it is clearly inappropriate in today's technological age to continue to charge people the same price for electricity 24-7
sentences.zh: 是的，在当今的技术时代，继续全天候向人们收取相同的电费显然是不合时宜的，

sentences.en: when the cost of providing people with electricity varies sometimes by orders of magnitude,
sentences.zh: 因为有时提供电力的成本会有几个数量级的差异，

sentences.en: depending on the time of day and the time of year and the grid conditions that apply.
sentences.zh: 这取决于一天中的时间、一年中的时间以及适用的电网状况。

sentences.en: So is it not then, by extension, also kind of dumb to not vary the price that we're paying customers who are generating solar power from their roofs?
sentences.zh: 那么，由此推论，不对那些在屋顶上发电的太阳能客户所支付的价格进行调整，难道不是也挺蠢的吗？

sentences.en: I agree with that as well.
sentences.zh: 我也同意这一点。

sentences.en: Don is the state's consumer advocate.
sentences.zh: 唐是州的消费者权益代言人。

sentences.en: His job is to watch out for people who pay electric bills.
sentences.zh: 他的工作是为支付电费的人保驾护航。

sentences.en: So basically, he's supposed to be keeping costs down and looking out for the little guy.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他应该负责压低成本并照顾普通老百姓。

sentences.en: It simply isn't fair to take a retired schoolteacher living on a fixed income in Manchester
sentences.zh: 让一个靠固定收入在曼彻斯特生活的退休教师，

sentences.en: and force that customer to pay subsidies to a wealthy hedge fund manager living in Bedford
sentences.zh: 去补贴一个住在贝德福德、屋顶铺满太阳能电池板的豪宅的富有对冲基金经理，这绝对是不公平的。

sentences.en: who has a McMansion that's covered in solar panels.
sentences.zh: 曼彻斯特真的有什么退休教师，贝德福德真的有什么对冲基金经理吗？

sentences.en: Is there some actual retired schoolteacher in Manchester and some actual hedge fund manager in Bedford?
sentences.zh: 因为迈克尔·哈灵顿给我的比喻完全一模一样。

sentences.en: Because Michael Harrington gave me the exact same analogy.
sentences.zh: 据我所知没有。

sentences.en: Not that I'm aware of.
sentences.zh: 绝对有。

sentences.en: There totally is.
sentences.zh: 那些人在哪？

sentences.en: Where are those people?
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，我是说，唐·克里夫也认为这种成本转移是个问题。

sentences.en: But anyway, I mean, Don Kreese also thinks that this cost-shifting thing is a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是唐·克里夫想要做的。

sentences.en: And so this is what Don Kreese wants to do.
sentences.zh: 这被称为分时电价。

sentences.en: It's called a time of use rate.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你的太阳能在电价高昂的时段（比如下午晚些时候）运行，你就能拿到更多报酬。

sentences.en: As in, you get paid more if your solar is going during those high-priced times, like later in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在下午消耗更多能量，你也要支付更多费用。

sentences.en: But you also pay more if you're using more energy in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 为了让这一点变得非常简单，每天都会有不同的价格。

sentences.en: And so to make this really simple, every day there'd be a different price.
sentences.zh: 下午2点到晚上8点之间价格更高，这段时间电价更贵。

sentences.en: A higher price between 2 p.m.
sentences.zh: 这为一种截然不同的能源支付方式打开了一扇缝隙。

sentences.en: and 8 p.m., which is when electricity is pricier.
sentences.zh: 它不再盲目遵循每个电子价值相同的疯狂错觉，

sentences.en: And this is cracking open the door to a radically different way to pay for energy.
sentences.zh: 而是承认当需求高时，电力就会变得昂贵。

sentences.en: Instead of abiding by this crazy illusion that every electron is worth the same amount,
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该让人们知道这一点。

sentences.en: it's acknowledging that when demand is high, electricity gets expensive.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以向消费者提供更频繁更新的信息。

sentences.en: And maybe we should let people know that.
sentences.zh: 这位是杰西卡·特兰西奇。

sentences.en: I think that we can provide that more frequently updated information to consumers.
sentences.zh: 她是麻省理工学院的能源研究教授。

sentences.en: So this is Jessica Trancic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这应该是可能的，对。

sentences.en: She's a professor of energy studies at MIT.
sentences.zh: 但她想把这推得更远。

sentences.en: I think that that should be possible, yeah.
sentences.zh: 记住，电价每五分钟都在不断变化。

sentences.en: But she wants to take it even a step farther.
sentences.zh: 她认为我们应该在家里装一个显示屏，上面写着，

sentences.en: Remember, there is constantly a new price for electricity every five minutes.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在的能源价格。

sentences.en: And she thinks we should have a display in our houses that says,
sentences.zh: 就像某种字面意义上的实时追踪？

sentences.en: here's the price of energy right now.
sentences.zh: 就像每五分钟市场结算一次，你就会得到一个新的价格？

sentences.en: Like something that literally follows?
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许按小时吧。

sentences.en: Like the five minute, every five minutes the market clears, you get a new price?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得五分钟可能有点太频繁了，但按小时可以。

sentences.en: Well, maybe hourly.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你能找到一家想这么做的公用事业公司，我随时准备加入。

sentences.en: You know, I think five minutes might be a bit too much, but hourly.
sentences.zh: 我会参加这个试点项目。

sentences.en: Well, so if you ever find a utility that wants to do that, I'm ready to sign up.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那会很有趣。

sentences.en: I'll be in the pilot.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: I think that'd be fun.
sentences.zh: 我会通知你的。

sentences.en: OK, great.
sentences.zh: 我会通知你的。

sentences.en: I'll let you know.
sentences.zh: 你看，我其实觉得这非常有趣，因为我根本不知道它会有所变化。

sentences.en: I'll let you know.
sentences.zh: 而且它的变化非常剧烈。

sentences.en: Now, see, I actually find that really interesting because I had no idea that it varied at all.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果有闪烁的红色高价警报之类的东西，我在打开电灯开关前会三思而后行。

sentences.en: And it varies wildly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, I would think twice about turning the light switch on if there was a flashing red high price alert or something.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种方法有一些非常重要的注意事项。

sentences.en: Yes, right.
sentences.zh: 首先，到处推广新电表成本高昂。

sentences.en: Now, there are some really important caveats to this approach.
sentences.zh: 这将是公用事业公司运营方式上一场巨大且可能非常艰难的变革。

sentences.en: For one, rolling out new meters everywhere would be expensive.
sentences.zh: 但其次，市场可能是残酷的。

sentences.en: And this would be a very big, maybe very difficult change in the way utilities operate.
sentences.zh: 有些价格会飙升到平均值的100倍，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But for two, the markets can be brutal.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么连杰西卡·特兰西奇都认为应该设置上限，也是为什么唐·克里夫想要一个稍微温和的版本，

sentences.en: There are prices that can go up like 100 times the average, which is crazy.
sentences.zh: 比如在下午2点到8点之间实行稍微贵一点的时段，

sentences.en: And that's why even Jessica Trancic thinks that they should have a cap and why Don Kreese wants this sort of declawed version of that,
sentences.zh: 而不是真正完全跟随市场。

sentences.en: which is like a slightly more expensive period from 2 to 8 p.m.
sentences.zh: 但他们都认为，是时候重新设计我们计量电力的方式了，因为太阳能让一切都变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: versus really following the markets.
sentences.zh: 这位是唐·克里夫。

sentences.en: But they both think that it's time we looked at redesigning the way our electricity is metered because solar has made everything more complicated.
sentences.zh: 你知道净计量电价是怎么开始的吗？

sentences.en: Here's Don Kreese.
sentences.zh: 当时在那个地方有个建筑师——

sentences.en: You know how net metering started?
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·斯特朗。

sentences.en: There was that architect guy in—
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Stephen Strong.
sentences.zh: 你真的跟他聊过吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我和他待了一天。

sentences.en: Did you actually talk to him?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I spent a day with him.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道，他根本没征求任何人的同意就直接这么做了。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 他不知道。

sentences.en: So you know that, like, he just did it without asking anybody's permission.
sentences.zh: 就像，我想看看如果我把我的建筑接上电线，并把它连接到波士顿爱迪生电网，我的电表会不会倒转。

sentences.en: He didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我想看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Like, I want to see if my meter is going to run backwards if I just wire my building up and, you know, and attach it to the Boston Edison grid.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。

sentences.en: I want to see what happens.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，你知道，这并不是说统一州法委员会聚在一起说，

sentences.en: And he was right.
sentences.zh: 让我们设计一部净计量法规，以这种非常合乎逻辑、严谨的方式促进分布式发电的发展。

sentences.en: But the fact is that it, you know, it wasn't like the Commission on Uniform State Laws got together and said,
sentences.zh: 不，这只是个意外。

sentences.en: let's design a net metering statute that will promote the development of distributed generation, you know, in this really logical, rigorous way.
sentences.zh: 现在它无处不在。

sentences.en: No, it just happened by accident.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都该好好看看，理性和精心设计的公共政策到底是什么样的。

sentences.en: And now it's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 或者也许我们只是回到按灯泡数量计费的时代。

sentences.en: And so it is high time for everybody to take a look and see what a rational, well-designed bit of public policy would be.
sentences.zh: 就这么办吧。

sentences.en: Or maybe we'll just go back to billing by the light bulb.
sentences.zh: 我要减少我的灯泡数量。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我，这就是。

sentences.en: I'm going to reduce my number of light bulbs.
sentences.zh: 我能，我能应付这个。

sentences.en: That's what I, that's.
sentences.zh: 那会很便宜。

sentences.en: I can, I can handle that.
